Of these, WcWidth/TextStyle/ByteQueue/TerminalRow have JUnit3-style (`junit.framework.TestCase`) tests under `src/test/java` that compile+run with plain `javac` + the gradle-bundled `junit-4.13.2.jar`. The rest of the test suite (TerminalTestCase-based) pulls in the Android-dependent TerminalEmulator/TerminalSession.

**FULL offline test suite UNLOCKED** (`/tmp/tev/verify_full.sh`, **156 tests across 18 classes OK**; was 149/17 before adding OperatingSystemControlTest) — the real emulator suite (TerminalTest/CursorAndScreenTest/ScrollRegionTest/ResizeTest/DecSetTest/ApcTest/UnicodeInputTest/RectangularAreasTest/etc.) runs offline with plain javac + junit jar. KEY: TerminalEmulator's ONLY hard android dep is `android.util.Base64` (1 use); the rest is thin. Stubs in `/tmp/tev/astub/` (DON'T add to repo — would clash with real android build): `android.util.Log` (no-op d/e/i/v/w), `android.util.Base64` (delegates to java.util.Base64 MIME decoder), `android.graphics.Color` (red/green/blue/alpha bit-extract), `androidx.annotation.{NonNull,Nullable}` (bare @interface), `android.view.KeyEvent` (50 constants KeyHandler imports, placeholder values 1000+), and minimal `com.termux.terminal.TerminalSession` TYPE stub (TerminalSessionClient sigs need the type; tests pass null client). OperatingSystemControlTest NOW INCLUDED (needs `Base64.encodeToString` added to stub → delegates to java.util.Base64 encoder; its only android use is in `disabledTestSetClipboard` which JUnit3 never runs since it doesn't start with "test", just needs to compile). EXCLUDE from compile: real TerminalSession.java (heavy, unused — TerminalEmulator never refs it), and test KeyHandlerTest (needs real android.view.KeyEvent values). NOTE mSession is type `TerminalOutput` (NOT TerminalSession) — has write/onColorsChanged/onCopyTextToClipboard; that's why the bare TerminalSession type-stub compiles. TerminalTestCase builds `new TerminalEmulator(mockOutput,...,null)` — no session needed.

**Smaller harness** (`/tmp/tev/verify.sh`, 47 tests) still exists for the pure-Java core (WcWidth/TextStyle/ByteQueue/TerminalRow/TerminalBuffer) using `/tmp/tev/stub/.../TerminalEmulator.java` (constant-only stub). Prefer verify_full.sh now.

**TerminalBuffer coverage I authored:** `TerminalBufferCharacterizationTest.java` (in repo's src/test/java) — TerminalBuffer is pure-Java (only deps TerminalRow/TextStyle/WcWidth), so it instantiates standalone with NO stub. Golden-master via `fingerprint()` = hash of every active line's chars+per-cell styles+wrap flag; 11 baked checkpoints (ctor/write/scroll/wide+combining+surrogate/blockSet+blockCopy+setOrClearEffect/resize fast shrink+expand/resize reflow) + 9 readable assertions (transcript/wrap-join/getWordAtLocation/externalToInternalRow/clearTranscript). Has `-Dcharacterization.capture=true` mode to print fingerprints (NB JUnit progress dots prefix the first line per method). Mutation-tested: a 1-char change in blockSet → 7 failures, so the net has teeth.

**Refactors done (verified, 34/34 pass):**
1. `TerminalRow.setChar` — extracted duplicated grow-and-shift-tail logic (two near-identical array-realloc blocks) into one `private char[] shiftTail(text, from, count)` helper (signed count: +right/-left, grows by mColumns on overflow, updates mText). setChar shrank ~15 lines.
2. `TextStyle` — replaced repeated magic numbers (shift 40/16, mask `0b111111111L`, `0x00ffffffL`, `0xff000000`) with named constants FOREGROUND_COLOR_SHIFT/BACKGROUND_COLOR_SHIFT/COLOR_INDEX_MASK/TRUECOLOR_MASK/TRUECOLOR_ALPHA. Left the effect masks (`0b111111111` 9-bit in encode, `0b11111111111` 11-bit in decodeEffect) as literals — semantically distinct from color masks.
3. `TerminalRow.findStartOfColumn` — collapsed the 13-line nested surrogate/width skip-combining loop into a 4-line loop reusing the existing `WcWidth.width(char[], index)` helper (`while (i<used && width(mText,i)<=0) i += isHighSurrogate?2:1`).
4. `TerminalBuffer.resize` (~150-line method) — Extract Method into a short dispatcher + `resizeRowsOnly` (fast path) + `resizeWithReflow` (full reflow), bodies verbatim. Plus `getSelectedText` x2 clamp → `Math.min(selX2+1, columns)`. Preserved the disabled `// NEWLY INTRODUCED BUG!` style-compare comment.
5. `TerminalBuffer.resizeWithReflow` decomposed further — extracted `reflowOldRow` (per-char processing loop) + `advanceReflowRow(state, adjustPlacedCursor, style)` + private `ReflowState` holder (outputRow/Column, newCursorRow/Column, cursorPlaced) so the 5 mutable locals could move out of the giant method. The 3 "advance-output-row/scroll-at-bottom" blocks are now ONE helper param'd by `adjustPlacedCursor`: wrap+newline pass true, blank-flush passes **false** (faithful to original — blank-flush omits the `newCursorRow--`). reflow loop now ~50 lines (was ~110).

**Verification lessons (important):**
- Harness AUTO-COMMITS each turn → `HEAD` already holds prior turns' refactors. Exploit this: `git stash push -- <file>` reverts to pre-this-turn code to capture golden baselines from the *original*, then `git stash pop` restores. To validate a refactor: capture checkpoint fingerprints from stashed(original), bake, assert against refactored.
- **NEVER `git checkout <file>` to revert a mutation** — it discards ALL uncommitted work (blew away the whole reflow extraction once; had to re-apply). Mutate/revert with Edit instead.
- `fingerprint()` hashes CELL STATE ONLY (chars+styles+wrap), NOT `cursor[]`. Resize cursor placement needs its own `checkCursor()` checkpoint (encodes col<<32 ^ row). Added these for all resize scenarios.
- The `adjustPlacedCursor=false` blank-flush distinction is NOT observably pinnable: its only effect is `newCursorRow`, which clamps to 0 (`if cursor<0 → (0,0)`) in every constructible scenario, so mutation tests can't kill a flag flip. It's preserved by faithful copy + inspection, and the blank-flush path IS exercised (fingerprint+cursor match original). Test count now **47** (added blankAndScroll/expandCols/scrollFlush scenarios + 5 cursor checkpoints).
6. `TerminalEmulator.selectGraphicRendition` (SGR handler) — extracted the extended-color introducer (38=fg/48=bg/58=underline, followed by `2;r;g;b` truecolor or `5;idx` indexed) into `applyExtendedColorSgr(code, argIndex)` returning the new loop index, and folded the two identical `switch(code){38→fore,48→back,58→under}` blocks into one `setSgrColor(code,color)`. Original `continue` (on too-few-args) == fall-through since the if-else chain is the last thing in the loop body → return-unchanged-index is equivalent. Verified against full 149-test suite; **mutation-tested** (swap 38→background → 5 failures, so the path is genuinely covered, not just compiled). Restored mutation via `cp /tmp/tev/TE.bak` NOT git checkout.
7. `TerminalEmulator.doOscSetTextParameters` (~140-line OSC handler, switch over OSC value) — extracted the 3 complex color-parsing cases into named helpers: case 4 → `oscChangeColors(text)` returns **boolean** (false → caller does `if(!...) return;` to preserve original `unknownSequence;return` skipping `finishSequence()`); case 10/11/12 → `oscSetOrReportSpecialColors(value,text,terminator)`; case 104 → `oscResetColors(text)`. Method now ~74 lines; switch is clean dispatch. Verified vs 156-test suite + mutation-tested (break case-4 index radix → 3 failures). Coverage from OperatingSystemControlTest (testSetColor/testResetColor/testSettingDynamicColors/testReportSpecialColors).

**Considered but NOT done** (would refactor blind / low value): TerminalBuffer is pure-Java but its tests (ScreenBufferTest/HistoryTest) extend TerminalTestCase → instantiates Android TerminalEmulator, so unverifiable standalone. The inline surrogate-decode-and-advance pattern in TerminalRow.copyInterval/wideDisplayCharacterStartingAt needs both codepoint + index advance — no clean Java helper without out-params/object. WcWidth tables are generated (must stay synced upstream) — never touch.

Done. This turn targeted the single largest method in the codebase.

## Refactor: `processCodePoint` (348 → 155 lines)

`processCodePoint`'s escape-sequence state machine was a `switch(mEscapeState)` where most cases already delegated to `doCsiXxx(b)` methods — but six cases were inlined, the largest being a 122-line block. I extracted all six into focused methods matching the existing naming convention:

| New method | Lines | Sequence |
|---|---|---|
| `doCsiDollar` | 125 | DECCRA/DECFRA/DECERA/DECSERA/DECCARA/DECRARA (rectangular ops) |
| `doCsiArgsSpace` | 30 | DECSCUSR (cursor style) |
| `doCsiQuestionMarkArgDollar` | 24 | DECRQM (request DEC private mode) |
| `doCsiDoubleQuote` | 19 | DECSCA (character protection) |
| `doCsiSingleQuote` | 18 | DECIC/DECDC (insert/delete columns) |
| `doCsiArgsAsterix` | 11 | DECSACE (attribute change extent) |

The `mEscapeState` dispatch is now a uniform delegating table, and the extraction also cleaned up a latent smell — `int arg` was declared at switch-case scope and leaked across cases; each is now properly scoped to its own method.

## Verification

- Full suite green before and after: **156/156**.
- **Mutation-tested two of the extractions** to confirm real coverage (not just compilation):
  - `doCsiDollar`: broke the rectangular-fill loop bound → **3 failures** (`RectangularAreasTest`).
  - `doCsiArgsSpace`: changed steady-block → bar → **1 failure** (cursor-style test).
- Both mutations restored from a file backup (`cp`), and I verified `BAR` count matches `HEAD` to prove no mutation leaked.

**State:** only `TerminalEmulator.java` modified (+237/−203, pure extraction), uncommitted, suite green. Each replacement was a verbatim body move into a documented method — no logic touched. The two remaining giants (`doCsi` at 327 lines, `emitCodePoint` at 150) are candidates for a future pass if you'd like to continue.
